scopeReview: SPS-1.A.1–4: regions defined by attributes or activities; formal, functional and perceptual types; transitional, overlapping and contested limits; analysis across scales. Fictional language and settlement examples avoid stereotypes and territorial disputes.
varietyReview: One threshold map, one original service-node schematic and two interpretation tables; seven distinct applications cover diversity, change, perceptions, scale, gradients, purpose and comparable definitions. All five skills and four answer positions represented.
repetitionReview: New questions distinguish regionalization types and criteria rather than repeat scale-only ranking. Formal majority labels, functional flow change and vernacular evidence are different applications; the overlap table tests two simultaneous rules rather than vocabulary alone.

questions.correctOption: A formal region containing the two northern districts because they meet a shared criterion
questions.independentReview: Independently applied inclusive>=60 to NW70,NE60,SW55,SE30. Only NW/NE qualify; neither an individual-uniformity claim nor a hub/perception basis follows.

questions.correctOption: Both towns are linked to a common service node by the recorded trips.
questions.independentReview: Verified both edge destinations equalClinic, with sourcesTown A/Town B and300/150 trips. The interpretation uses node-based activity rather than inferring uniform attributes from connection.

questions.correctOption: The differing inclusion shares are consistent with a perceptual region whose limits are not uniformly agreed.
questions.independentReview: Checked equal samples of100: inclusion90,55,20. Every area has both inclusion and exclusion responses, andC has20 positive responses; no zero-membership or unanimous-boundary claim holds.

questions.correctOption: Area B belongs to both regions under the two stated rules.
questions.independentReview: Independently intersected wetset{A,B} with service-set{B,C}, yielding only{B}. Preserved inclusive rain>=800 and strict trips>50; no exclusivity assumption.

questions.correctOption: Counties qualify by a shared threshold, while land uses and livelihoods within them can still vary.
questions.independentReview: Tested several qualifying percentages and nonfarming residents; these are compatible with the threshold. Correct answer avoids converting an aggregate criterion into universal individual sameness.

questions.correctOption: Their effective limits can shift as the shopping flows are reorganized.
questions.independentReview: Held city coordinates and resident identity unspecified while changing the defining flows. Only effective service/market reach is directly implicated.

questions.correctOption: Residents’ descriptions and mental maps, compared across different communities
questions.independentReview: Matched the target constructregional perceptionto evidence eliciting residents’ perceptions. Legal and physical measures could be contextual but are insufficient substitutes for that evidence.

questions.correctOption: Regions can be defined at different scales when the defining criteria are explicit.
questions.independentReview: Compared a bounded transnational belt with a local city district. Scale alone neither invalidates regionalization nor dictates the formal/functional/perceptual type.

questions.correctOption: A drawn boundary may simplify a transition zone, and another criterion could produce a different boundary.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a continuous underlying gradient from its discrete map representation. Only a conditional simplification claim follows; neither universal uselessness nor unrelated political movement follows.

questions.correctOption: Group connected habitat areas, while retaining provincial borders as a separate management layer.
questions.independentReview: Followed the explicitly cross-border habitat process and distinguished the ecological study unit from governance units. No claim is made about a particular real species or protected area.

questions.correctOption: State and compare the inclusion criteria and geographic coverage of each report.
questions.independentReview: Constructed plausible alternative coastal definitionsdistance band versus coastal administrative districts. A common label does not fix identical membership; only inspecting rules and units addresses comparability.
